summary: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions.
takeaways: Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions.

Across 52,920 reports from 7B and 8B models spanning 120 tasks, four doses and three prompts, pain reports never exceeded what altered text revealed: exact-test bounds placed the excess below 2.5 percentage points in 106 of 108 emotion conditions and below 3.9 in all.
We tested whether three open-weight models from two families, including two Qwen models with the original adapters, could report this state.
